course: Industry 4.0 and Industrial Internet of Things
week_title: Industrial Internet Reference Architecture (IIRA) & IIoT Business Models
topic_overview: Focuses on IIRA 4 Viewpoints (Business, Usage, Functional, Implementation), 5 Functional Domains, 3-Tier Architecture Pattern (Edge, Platform, Enterprise), utility business models (Product-as-a-Service, Pay-per-Use, Asset Sharing), and commercial IIoT platforms/testbeds.

topics.topic_name: Industrial Internet Reference Architecture (IIRA) Overview & Viewpoints
topics.topic_description: Examines the 4 IIRA viewpoints defined by the Industrial Internet Consortium (IIC): Business, Usage, Functional, and Implementation Viewpoints.

questions.question: Which consortium published the Industrial Internet Reference Architecture (IIRA)?
questions.justification: The Industrial Internet Consortium (IIC) developed and published the IIRA framework.

questions.question: How many fundamental Viewpoints are defined in the IIRA architecture model?
questions.justification: IIRA defines 4 primary Viewpoints: Business, Usage, Functional, and Implementation Viewpoints.

questions.question: Which IIRA Viewpoint identifies the business stakeholders, business vision, return on investment (ROI), and high-level objectives?
questions.justification: The Business Viewpoint addresses commercial vision, stakeholder needs, value propositions, and economic metrics.

questions.question: A system designer drafts sequence diagrams and interaction workflows illustrating how human operators and automated agents execute operational tasks. Which IIRA Viewpoint does this represent?
questions.justification: The Usage Viewpoint models expected system behavior, operational workflows, usage scenarios, and interaction sequences.

questions.question: Which IIRA Viewpoint details functional component blocks, data flows, and control interfaces without specifying vendor hardware technologies?
questions.justification: The Functional Viewpoint structures functional domains (Control, Operations, Information, Application, Business) abstractly.

questions.question: Which IIRA Viewpoint details the software packages, network switches, cabling, and hardware servers deployed in a factory?
questions.justification: The Implementation Viewpoint specifies physical hardware, software stacks, topology, and execution technologies.

topics.topic_name: IIRA Functional Domains (Control, Operations, Information, Application, Business)
topics.topic_description: Details the 5 functional domains of IIRA: Control Domain, Operations Domain, Information Domain, Application Domain, and Business Domain.

questions.question: In the IIRA Functional Domain model, which domain directly interfaces with physical sensors and actuators to execute sense-actuate loops?
questions.justification: The Control Domain contains sensing, actuation, communication, and local closed-loop control elements.

questions.question: Which IIRA functional domain handles data ingestion, transformations, analytics algorithms, and digital twin state modeling?
questions.justification: The Information Domain manages data collection, transformation, analytics processing, and data persistence.

questions.question: Asset health monitoring, fleet management, diagnostic provisioning, and maintenance scheduling reside in which IIRA functional domain?
questions.justification: The Operations Domain provides operational management functions including maintenance, monitoring, asset management, and provisioning.

questions.question: A smart factory platform connects high-level enterprise ERP and CRM systems with operational analytics engines. Which IIRA domain encapsulates these enterprise business logic rules?
questions.justification: The Business Domain manages enterprise business functions, customer relationship integration, order execution, and financial logic.

questions.question: How does data flow between the Control Domain and the Information Domain across the IIRA functional architecture?

options.A: Sensors emit raw telemetry through communication gateways up to the Information domain, while analytical control setpoints flow back down
options.B: Data flows only from left to right using printed paper logs
options.C: Control domain data is permanently stored inside the physical motor windings
options.D: No communication is allowed between domains

questions.justification: Telemetry moves upward from Control to Information/Application domains, while control setpoints and optimizations flow back down.

questions.question: In the IIRA Functional Architecture, which domain provides APIs and user interfaces for human operators to monitor shop-floor operations?
questions.justification: The Application Domain encapsulates user interfaces, business logic APIs, and operator interaction dashboards.

topics.topic_name: IIRA Implementation Viewpoint & Three-Tier Architecture Pattern
topics.topic_description: Examines the Three-Tier Architecture Pattern: Edge Tier, Platform Tier, and Enterprise Tier.

questions.question: What are the three tiers in the classic IIRA Three-Tier Architecture Pattern?

options.B: Edge Tier, Platform Tier, Enterprise Tier

questions.justification: The three tiers are the Edge Tier (proximity to assets), Platform Tier (data consolidation/analytics), and Enterprise Tier (business applications).

questions.question: Which tier in the IIRA Implementation Architecture contains physical machines, field gateways, and real-time edge microcontrollers?
questions.justification: The Edge Tier comprises physical assets, local sensors/actuators, and edge processing gateways.

questions.question: Which tier consolidates data across multiple edge sites, executes query processing, and provides cloud analytics platforms?
questions.justification: The Platform Tier receives edge data, executes intermediate analytics, handles device management, and routes insights.

questions.question: An enterprise runs localized real-time safety control loops on an edge gateway (latency < 2ms) and sends aggregated hourly health summaries to a cloud platform for long-term predictive models. Which tier handles each task?

options.A: Edge Tier handles real-time safety; Platform Tier handles cloud predictive models
options.B: Platform Tier handles real-time safety; Enterprise Tier handles mechanical valves
options.C: Enterprise Tier handles microsecond control; Edge Tier handles payroll
options.D: Edge Tier handles global ERP; Platform Tier handles copper wiring

questions.justification: Time-critical low-latency control runs at the Edge Tier, while multi-site analytics run at the Platform Tier.

questions.question: Where do domain-specific executive dashboards, ERP integrations, and customer portals reside in the Three-Tier pattern?
questions.justification: Enterprise-level business applications, executive portals, and ERP connections sit within the Enterprise Tier.

questions.question: Which network boundary in the IIRA Three-Tier pattern connects the Edge Tier to the Platform Tier across wide area networks?
questions.justification: The Access Network bridges field edge gateways (Edge Tier) to cloud platforms (Platform Tier) over cellular/WAN links.

topics.topic_name: Utility-Driven IIoT Business Models (Pay-per-Use, Asset Sharing, PaaS)
topics.topic_description: Covers innovative IIoT monetization strategies: Outcome-Based Pricing, Asset Sharing, Product-as-a-Service, and Pay-per-X utility models.

questions.question: In a 'Pay-per-Use' IIoT business model, how does a customer pay the equipment provider?

options.A: A fixed upfront lump sum purchase price
options.B: Based on actual operational metrics (e.g., operating hours, units produced, or cubic meters delivered)
options.C: By transferring equity shares in their company
options.D: Through manual barter of raw materials

questions.justification: Pay-per-use bills customers strictly according to measured telemetry usage.

questions.question: In Kaeser Compressors' famous 'Sigma Air Utility' business model, what is sold to end-user factories?

options.B: Compressed air delivered as a measured service ($/m³ of air) (OPEX)

questions.justification: Kaeser sells compressed air as a measured utility service rather than selling compressor hardware.

questions.question: What is 'Asset Sharing' in an industrial IIoT ecosystem?

options.A: Scrapping old machinery for metal recycling
options.B: Multiple companies sharing high-cost capital assets (e.g., specialized testbeds or heavy equipment) via IIoT scheduling platforms
options.D: Using one battery to power two factories

questions.justification: Asset sharing maximizes equipment utilization by making expensive machinery available to multiple users via digital scheduling.

questions.question: Why does an equipment vendor assume greater operational risk under an Outcome-Based SLA model, and how does IIoT mitigate this risk?

options.A: The vendor bears maintenance risks, but continuous IIoT telemetry enables predictive maintenance to prevent unexpected failures
options.C: IIoT eliminates all friction in mechanical gears
options.D: The vendor shifts all power grid costs to electricity companies

questions.justification: Under outcome-based contracts, machine downtime penalizes the vendor; telemetry provides early failure warnings to maintain uptime.

questions.question: How does an IIoT Product-as-a-Service model align the financial incentives of the equipment vendor and the factory customer?

options.A: Both profit when the equipment operates efficiently with minimal breakdown and low energy consumption
options.B: The vendor profits most when the machine breaks down frequently
options.C: The customer pays higher fees when the machine is broken

questions.justification: Since the vendor incurs maintenance costs while the customer relies on reliable output, both benefit from peak efficiency and high reliability.

questions.question: How does an 'Equipment Sharing' digital platform increase capital asset efficiency for small and medium enterprises (SMEs)?

options.A: By allowing SMEs to rent unused capacity on high-cost specialized machinery on-demand rather than buying dedicated machines
options.B: By forcing SMEs to buy duplicate machines
options.C: By shutting down machinery during weekdays

questions.justification: Digital asset sharing platforms democratize access to expensive capital equipment through flexible multi-tenant scheduling.

topics.topic_name: Commercial IIoT Platforms & Testbeds (GE Predix, Lumada, MindSphere)
topics.topic_description: Examines commercial IIoT platforms (GE Predix, Hitachi Lumada, Siemens MindSphere) and IIC-sponsored testbeds (Track and Trace, Smart Grid, Microgrid).

questions.question: What is the primary role of an Industrial IoT platform like GE Predix, Hitachi Lumada, or Siemens MindSphere?

options.B: To provide cloud connectivity, asset health monitoring, device management, and industrial analytics

questions.justification: IIoT platforms serve as cloud/edge middleware operating systems connecting field assets with advanced analytics.

questions.question: What is an 'IIC Testbed'?

options.A: A physical mattress used in factory resting rooms
options.B: A controlled experimentation environment where IIoT technologies, standards, and architectures are tested in real-world scenarios
options.C: A software game for factory workers
options.D: A laboratory for testing chemical soil fertilizers

questions.justification: IIC Testbeds serve as rigorous real-world test environments to validate architectures, interoperability, and business value.

questions.question: Which IIC Testbed focuses on real-time tracking of high-value tools, assets, and parts across industrial factory floors?
questions.justification: The Track and Trace testbed validates location tracking and asset status monitoring across manufacturing and supply chains.

questions.question: How does Hitachi's Lumada platform utilize 'Lumada Asset Avatars' (Digital Twins) to optimize factory maintenance?

options.A: By displaying 3D cartoon animations for video games
options.B: By maintaining virtual digital twin models that sync with real-time asset telemetry to simulate performance and predict failures

questions.justification: Asset Avatars act as digital twin representations continuously updated via asset sensors to simulate and optimize health.

questions.question: Why are multi-vendor interoperability standards tested heavily in IIC testbeds before enterprise rollout?

options.A: To ensure sensors, gateways, and cloud platforms from different vendors can exchange data without proprietary lock-in
options.B: To force all factories to buy from a single hardware supplier
options.C: Because multi-vendor systems never require network cables
options.D: To replace TCP/IP with analog telegraph signals

questions.justification: Interoperability validation ensures open data exchange across heterogeneous vendor hardware and software components.

questions.question: What primary technical capability is validated in the IIC Microgrid Testbed?

options.A: Autonomous control, real-time demand-response, and seamless transition between grid-tied and islanded modes using multi-vendor controllers

questions.justification: Microgrid testbeds validate interoperability, islanding transitions, and distributed renewable energy control algorithms.
